10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c04307.abstract: Abstract Magnetoresistive effects are typically symmetric under magnetization reversal. However, nonlinear spin transport can give rise to unidirectional magnetoresistance in systems with strong spin–orbit interaction and broken inversion symmetry. Here, we report a large magnonic unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance (USMR) in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS4 in contact with Pt, driven by the nonequilibrium magnon accumulation with a finite magnon chemical potential. In contrast to conventional magnonic USMR driven by magnetization fluctuations, this effect persists under strong magnetic fields and low temperatures. The magnitude of magnonic USMR in CrPS4/Pt exceeds that of YIG/Pt by more than 2 orders of magnitude and surpasses the electrical USMR in metallic Ta/Co bilayers by a factor of 2. Our results highlight magnon chemical potential gradients for nonlinear magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic van der Waals heterostructures and open a route to magnon-based antiferromagnetic spintronic functionalities in two-terminal device geometries.
10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c04307.title: Unidirectional Magnetoresistance Driven by Nonequilibrium Antiferromagnetic Magnons

10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174602.abstract: k π -skyrmions are topological magnetic textures with promising applications in spintronic devices. In this work, we investigated the stability and current-driven dynamics of k π -skyrmions ( k = 1,2,3 , and 4) in racetrack nanostructures. Stability phase diagrams were constructed as a function of the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction strength ( D int ) and the perpendicular magnetic field ( B z ). Our results showed that the stabilization range of each k π -skyrmion strongly depends on D int . In addition, the diameters of all textures increased with increasing D int and decreased with increasing B z . The current-driven dynamics induced by spin–orbit torque were then investigated. Our results showed that the velocity of all k π -skyrmions increased with current density and decreased with perpendicular magnetic field. Although the 3 π -skyrmion exhibited larger longitudinal velocities during the transient regime than the π -skyrmion, both textures reached nearly identical steady-state velocities. A similar behavior was observed for the 2 π - and 4 π -skyrmions. The steady-state dynamics were further analyzed using the Thiele formalism, which reproduced the trends observed in the micromagnetic simulations. These findings provide insight into the stabilization and transport properties of k π -skyrmions and support their potential use in future spintronic applications.
10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174602.title: Spin orbit torque manipulation of kπ-skyrmions in racetrack nanostructures for spintronic memory applications

10.1103/nny3-5mnz.abstract: We theoretically investigate the chaotic behavior of spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance in magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy under thermal fluctuations. By calculating the Lyapunov exponent based on the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation, we demonstrate that an MTJ characterized by a double-well potential, composed of uniaxial magnetic anisotropy and an external dc magnetic field, exhibits chaotic magnetization dynamics that can be controlled by means of the dc bias via spin-transfer torque. Furthermore, we find that thermal fluctuations help to induce these chaotic magnetization dynamics, which can be regarded as noise-induced chaos. This research provides a basis for brain-inspired computing using spintronic devices and advances the understanding of the interplay between thermal fluctuations and chaos in magnetization dynamics.
10.1103/nny3-5mnz.title: Current-control of chaos and effects of thermal fluctuations in magnetic tunnel junctions
